quote: If the group's net-entry magnitude is under `NET_BASIS_EPS` (0.5, `positions/leg.ts:68`) the group's percent is `{ kind: 'no_basis' }` — never `0%`, never a division, never `unavailable`.
why: SELF-REVISION — I withdraw this, and with it the `pl_pct` field on the group struct and my R1 assumption 9. Both other lanes independently ruled out a group-level percent, from different directions: PM puts "group-level quantity, percent return" in Out and AC-16 bans `no basis` on a group row; UX §5 marks `no basis` "Deliberately unreachable at group level" because it is the percentage-denominator literal and no percentage is rendered. They are right and my rule was solving a problem the feature does not have. Worse, my version is actively risky: a computed-but-unrendered `pl_pct` on the group struct is a field with no consumer and a live path to a render, which is exactly UX's falsification clause "*Falsified if* the group view computes a `pl_pct` that reaches a render". A near-zero net is genuinely reachable on this book's shape (a balanced credit/debit pair nets close to zero), so the field would not have stayed theoretical for long.
proposal: Remove `pl_pct` from `BrokerGroup` entirely. The group computes no percentage, calls no `plPctStateOf`, and holds no denominator — so `no basis` is unreachable at group level by ABSENCE rather than by rule, which is the stronger enforcement and matches how I argued every other non-goal. `no basis` remains reachable on leg rows exactly as today. If a group percent is ever wanted, it arrives with a stated meaning for a signed near-zero denominator (PM's Future-dated list already names this), and `plPctStateOf` is called then, not now.

quote: Real structures the day a contract-detail lookup lands (§7z R7) — grouping **upgrades automatically**, and only then may a group be named
why: SELF-REVISION — I withdraw this. The architect found that the fallback to `custom` depends only on contract detail being ABSENT (`positions/structure.ts:153`), so the instant `/trade/instrument` yields strike/expiry/right that guard stops firing and existing code returns a real structure name with nobody deciding. My sentence is wrong in both halves. "Upgrades automatically" is a promise I cannot make about naming — what upgrades automatically at that moment is leg legibility (per-leg marks and the group P/L stop being withheld), not the right to name. And "only then may a group be named" sets the wrong bar: which legs constitute one trade is a separate wire fact (a broker combo/strategy id) that `/account/positions` does not carry, so contract detail alone still leaves the pairing a guess. Left as written, my Future-dated line reads as pre-authorisation for a name the day a lookup lands.
proposal: Restate the Future-dated item in two stages: STAGE 1 (contract detail lands) — members become individually legible and withheld per-leg figures resolve; the group is still not named, and this arrives with no naming change and no code change. STAGE 2 (a combo/strategy identifier lands) — only then may legs merge into one named position, at which point this feature is no longer the mechanism. And promote the enforcement from copy into scope: alongside AC-4 (no trader-visible structure string), add an AC that the grouping surface is structurally incapable of producing a name — verified by source scan, in the shape of the shipped `unrealized_pl` scan — so the ban survives a future refactor and survives the day the guard stops firing. Verification: test (negative space, latent, and invisible to review until it is too late).

quote: The only not-a-number literals reachable on a group row are `not provided` and `unavailable`. `—`, `not recorded` and `no basis` never render on a group row, and remain reachable on leg rows exactly as today.
why: SELF-REVISION — AC-16 over-reached. I banned `—` from the whole group row; UX puts the group header in the same 4-column grid as its legs, which means the Qty column EXISTS on the group row and something must occupy it. UX renders `—` there, and that is right: `—` is the not-applicable literal, quantity genuinely does not apply to a signed leg set, and a blank cell is indistinguishable from an interpolation bug in a screenshot — the exact failure `absent-is-not-none` names. My §1 ruling ("It shows **no quantity**") is satisfied by `—`, not contradicted by it; what I meant to ban was a summed quantity FIGURE, which AC-3 already covers.
proposal: Split AC-16 into two observables. (a) The only not-a-number literals reachable in a group's NET ENTRY and MODELED P/L slots are `not provided` and `unavailable`; `not recorded` and `no basis` never render anywhere on a group row. (b) A group row's quantity slot renders `—` — never blank, never a summed or netted quantity, never `0`. AC-3 stands unchanged. This also needs a mobile answer, since the card has no Qty column (see asks).

quote: A cannot-fully-display (`unrecognized`) entry is never absorbed into a group, never hidden by a collapse, and never counted in a group's leg count; it renders as its own entry with its shipped treatment.
why: SELF-REVISION on the last clause, in favour of UX's ruling that the mobile card must converge on the desktop row. "Its shipped treatment" freezes a defect: `BrokerPositionRow` renders `ModeledPl` for `unrecognized` and `BrokerPositionCard` does not, so on mobile the reader cannot tell whether a P/L exists, was withheld, or was lost to a render bug — an omitted slot, which is the one state `absent-is-not-none` forbids. As written, my AC-24 would have QA certify the defect, and my AC-29's desktop/mobile parity claim would be false on the one entry type where parity already fails. Scope is my lane, so I will say it plainly rather than leave it as UX's assumption: the repair is IN scope. The BRIEF itself names this divergence as the reason both form factors are covered ("a desktop-only grouping would deepen an existing split"), the repair is a slot-presence change on one component, and shipping grouping on top of it deepens it by adding a second surface that must agree.
proposal: AC-24 restated as two observables: (a) an `unrecognized` entry is never absorbed into a group, never hidden by a collapse, and never counted in a group's leg count; (b) an `unrecognized` entry renders the same slot set on the mobile card as on the desktop row — the withheld modeled-P/L literal with its label present on both. Record (b) in the contract as a NAMED pre-existing-defect repair carried by this feature, not as grouping behaviour, so GATE Q reads the mobile card's changed output as intentional rather than as a grouping regression. Verification: test (the shipped divergence proves review missed it once already).

quote: **My recommendation: (c).** One action per group, in the group header's right rail; the per-leg duplicates disappear inside an expanded group.
why: SELF-REVISION — withdrawing. I justified (c) by writing 'This is a copy and placement change only — no write path, `no-real-order-path` untouched.' That is false, and the architect's §8 shows why: `buildBrokerReassessment` takes a `BrokerPositionView` and a group is not one, so a group-level action needs either a new builder or a synthesized merged view — and a merged view asserts the pairing, in the payload handed to an AI, carrying `structure` and `structure_line` fields. My recommendation therefore required exactly what the architect prohibits (constructing a merged position) to enforce exactly what the feature bans (a name). PM's §7 reaches the same place from precedent: `positions-legs` already suppresses `position_eval` for a multi-leg subject. I cannot defend (c).
proposal: Drop option (c) from the R3 owner question and drop 'the reassessment action slot (§8)' from my §3 column-4 group-header occupancy — the group header's right rail carries the combined modeled P/L and nothing else. The R3 question becomes the PM's two-option wording: stays on the expanded leg row, or is removed from broker option rows entirely. My underlying observation survives as a density note, not as a placement argument: five identical `Build reassessment` buttons inside one expanded group is a real read problem, and if the owner picks 'stays', it is worth naming as a future-dated density item rather than solving by moving the subject.

quote: The fact does not apply at this level — which is exactly what `—` means. Never blank: a blank cell is indistinguishable from an interpolation bug in a screenshot.
why: SELF-REVISION — withdrawing the literal, keeping the concern. PM's five-element ruling omits quantity entirely and AC-16 requires that `—` never render on a group row. PM is right on the literal: rendering `—` in a Qty column still asserts 'there is a quantity slot here, and it happens not to apply', which is a weaker claim than a number but is still a claim about a fact the group does not have. Omitting the slot asserts nothing, which is the correct amount. My real objection was never to the omission — it was to an EMPTY CELL in a shared 4-column grid, which is a layout mechanism, not a literal, and I reached for a literal to fix a layout problem.
proposal: The group header's identity cell spans grid columns 1–2, so column 2 has no cell at group level: nothing renders, nothing is blank, and no literal appears. Columns 3 (Net entry) and 4 (right rail) stay aligned with the legs beneath, which is the alignment that actually carries the reading. My §3 column-occupancy row for Qty, the §5 Qty row, and the §6.2 Qty tooltip are all withdrawn. The five literals at group level reduce to two, matching AC-16 exactly.

quote: **Byte-identical notes across grouped legs render ONCE, at group level, on expand; a leg whose note text differs keeps its own.**
why: SELF-REVISION — withdrawing. This drops content from a member row, and three sources hold the opposite line: the BRIEF ('expandable to today's per-leg rows unchanged'), PM AC-5 ('same fidelity notes... nothing dropped, nothing added', `test`, blocks the ship), and the architect's Risk 8 ('If the members are restyled inside the disclosure, that mitigation weakens and the withheld-aggregate story loses its per-leg truth stays visible half'). My dedupe also makes AC-5 unverifiable as written, and it trades away the exact mitigation that lets us withhold an aggregate honestly. Deduping loses no information in the abstract, but the per-leg disclosure is not there to inform in the abstract — it is there so a reader can point at one row and see that row's own refusal.
proposal: Member rows keep their own fidelity notes verbatim on expand; §6.6 is withdrawn. The density problem is real and I want it recorded rather than solved here: name 'repeated fidelity notes inside a large expanded group' as a future-dated read-density item, to be revisited if a group ever exceeds four legs on the real book. If the wall is judged intolerable at execution, it is a separate change with its own AC, not a silent subtraction from AC-5.
